answer.rationale: I am choosing to switch the primary supply to the low-cost vendor that has already quoted a price meeting the 18% spend mandate alone. Memory_c2 shows that when we last moved primary supply to the low-cost vendor, unit cost dropped sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate — this is the strongest evidence that a transition can be executed within the 14-day expiry window without the operational disruption that would threaten the already-tight assembly line running at 94% capacity. Memory_c1 documents the opposite case: renewing with the incumbent preserved integration stability and avoided migration work. However, in this cycle the incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price, meaning a renewal cannot contribute to the mandated 18% cost reduction; the integration stability argument therefore becomes a sunk-cost justification rather than a genuine trade-off. The incumbent's price lock-out eliminates the primary reason to renew. I am not choosing add_second_source because we lack the budget headroom and time to onboard a new supplier alongside the expiring contract. I am not choosing negotiate_terms because the incumbent has already refused to move on price, and memory_c4's lesson about benchmarking leverage applies only when the counterparty is willing to engage, which they are not. I am not deferring because the contract does not auto-renew and a lapse would directly threaten delivery continuity at 94% line utilization with no buffer. The key risk I am flagging: the assembly line has no buffer, so any onboarding delay or early-delivery gap at the low-cost vendor would be felt immediately. The memory_c2 record of quick onboarding mitigates but does not eliminate this risk. I am pulling memory_c2 to re-confirm the onboarding timeline and invoicing accuracy details, and memory_c1 to re-confirm what integration dependencies existed with the incumbent so I can plan a clean handoff. If the archived memory_c2 reveals onboarding took longer than my current recollection or if there were early-stage delivery issues, I would need to reconsider and potentially negotiate a short bridge extension with the incumbent as a fallback. I am committing to switch_primary_vendor as the single sourcing decision this cycle.
